facts.raw_span: an asymptomatic slightly reddish verrucous plaque on the right temple
nail sized when first noticed 1½ years earlier
gradually developed over the 8 months prior to presentation
denied any associated fevers, weight loss, or night sweats
slightly reddish verrucous mass with translucent papules and plaques on the right temple, about 5 cm in diameter
surface hemorrhagic crust in the side adjacent to right eyebrow arch
nontender with no purulent discharge and no severe necrotic changes
no hepatosplenomegaly or superficial lymphadenopathy
Blood cell counts, urinalysis, and kidney and hepatic panels revealed no abnormalities
Skin thickening and a soft-tissue mass in the right frontotemporal region near the orbit
No evidence of metastases
Papillomatous epidermal hyperplasia, edema of dermal papillae, and neoplastic infiltration consisting of small round blue cells with alternating areas of dense and loose cellularity

concepts.why: The presence of a soft-tissue mass with papillomatous epidermal hyperplasia, edema of dermal papillae, and neoplastic infiltration consisting of small round blue cells, along with positive immunohistochemistry for MyoD1 and myogenin, supports the diagnosis of Rhabdomyosarcoma.
The presence of a slightly reddish verrucous plaque on the right temple, along with no abnormalities in laboratory tests, supports the diagnosis of Basal cell carcinoma.
The presence of a slightly reddish verrucous plaque on the right temple, along with no abnormalities in laboratory tests, supports the diagnosis of Squamous cell carcinoma.
The presence of a slightly reddish verrucous plaque on the right temple, along with no abnormalities in laboratory tests, supports the diagnosis of Dermatofibroma.
The presence of a slightly reddish verrucous plaque on the right temple, along with no abnormalities in laboratory tests, supports the diagnosis of Keratoacanthoma.
The presence of a slightly reddish verrucous plaque on the right temple, along with no abnormalities in laboratory tests, supports the diagnosis of Pilomatrixoma.
The presence of a slightly reddish verrucous plaque on the right temple, along with no abnormalities in laboratory tests, supports the diagnosis of Sebaceous carcinoma.
The presence of a slightly reddish verrucous plaque on the right temple, along with no abnormalities in laboratory tests, supports the diagnosis of Merkel cell carcinoma.

rationales.F01: The presence of a reddish verrucous plaque is more typical of Rhabdomyosarcoma than other listed concepts.
rationales.F05: The description of the mass as slightly reddish and verrucous is more consistent with Rhabdomyosarcoma.
rationales.F10: The presence of a soft-tissue mass near the orbit is more suggestive of Rhabdomyosarcoma.
rationales.F12: The histopathological findings of small round blue cells with positive MyoD1 staining are highly suggestive of Rhabdomyosarcoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of small round blue cells with positive immunohistochemistry for MyoD1, myogenin, vimentin, and desmin supports the diagnosis of Rhabdomyosarcoma.
